title: OTLP rate-control and log archival playbook
summary: Working playbook for deploying OTEL collectors and Prometheus/Grafana components in VPC/on-prem environments focusing on rate control (batching, compression, backpressure) and durable log archival to S3-compatible stores. Includes terraform notes, upgrade path, canary plan, and rollback guidance.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an actionable playbook for private deployments where network egress and storage are constrained. We define conservative defaults for OTLP batching, compression and rate control, outline reliable log archival (S3-compatible + lifecycle policies), and provide an upgrade path from legacy fluentd/rsyslog agents to consolidated OTEL + Prometheus remote_write setup.

Context & constraints:
- Target environments: VPC-hosted customer deployments and on-prem racks with restricted outbound bandwidth and private S3 endpoints.
- Requirements: low 99th-percentile tail latency for RPCs; avoid OTEL collector OOMs under bursty logs; guarantees on log durability (7d hot, 365d cold via object storage).
- Compliance: support KMS-encrypted object storage and customer-provided TLS certs.

High-level architecture (textual):
- App pods -> local sidecar/daemonset OTEL collector (batching enabled) -> regional OTEL gateway (stateful, autoscaled) -> forward to: Prometheus remote_write (via agent), Grafana metrics ingest, and log-archive worker that writes to S3-compatible endpoint with multipart + retry.

Key principles:
1) Push backpressure to the edge: sidecar collectors should throttle at pod-level to protect node memory/CPU.
2) Prefer batching + compression over unbounded concurrent writes.
3) Use durable handoff for logs when network unavailable (disk-buffering with bounded size and oldest-first eviction).
4) Make Terraform modules idempotent and parameterized for network egress policies (NAT, proxy), S3 endpoints, and certs.

Operational knobs (recommended defaults):
- otel_collector.batch.timeout: 200ms
- otel_collector.batch.send_batch_size: 1024 (max items)
- otel_collector.batch.send_batch_max_bytes: 1_048_576 (1MB)
- otel_collector.queue.max_items: 50_000 (depends on disk quota; set lower for constrained nodes)
- compression: gzip level 3 on OTLP/gRPC path to gateway
- concurrency: max 8 concurrent uploads per collector to gateway
- retry_policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max elapsed 30m

S3 archival policy (recommended):
- Put objects with prefix: <customer-id>/logs/yyyy-mm-dd/HHMMSS-<uuid>.ndjson.gz
- Lifecycle: transition to cold storage after 14d, expire after 395d
- Server-side encryption: customer KMS key enforced at bucket policy

Terraform module notes (summary, see terraform_notes for details):
- Modules: private_deployments/otlp-collector, private_deployments/otlp-gateway, private_deployments/log-archiver, private_deployments/grafana-provisioner, private_deployments/prom-remote-write
- Use input variable `egress_proxy` to toggle NAT vs proxy routing
- Provide `s3_endpoint` and `s3_ca_cert` when using on-prem object storage

Change window and SLOs:
- Recommended maintenance window: 02:00-06:00 UTC to minimize overlap with customer peak in NA/EU.
- SLOs to watch during rollout: 99p token latency for hosted APIs that rely on metrics should not degrade > 10%. Log ingest success rate target: >= 99.5% over 1h after rollout.

Unresolved questions (todo):
- Disk-buffer eviction policy preference: oldest-first vs largest-first for mixed size events.
- Fine-grain RBAC for archiver worker when using customer-managed S3 with role assumption.

Notes-to-self:
- Validate gzip compression benefits on 2 representative customers with high-cardinality logs; measure CPU tradeoff.
terraform_notes:
Overview:
We intentionally keep modules small and composable. Each module exposes a `deploy_mode` (daemonset | sidecar | gateway) plus `resource_profile` (small|medium|large).

Module-specific knobs (practical):
- otlp-collector module:
  - var.deploy_mode: daemonset
  - var.batch_timeout_ms: default 200
  - var.queue_max_items: default 50000
  - var.disk_buffer_path: /var/lib/otel-buffer
  - var.disk_buffer_max_size_mb: 10240
  - var.image_tag: pinned to semver for upgrades

- otlp-gateway module:
  - module creates a statefulset behind a headless service; expose `replica_count` and `pdb.min_available`.
  - var.proxy_auth_secret: optional (used when egress proxy required)

- log-archiver module:
  - uses k8s CronJob for daily compaction + uploader and a Deployment for continuous archival.
  - var.s3_endpoint / var.s3_region / var.kms_key_id must be set for production.

Providers & policy considerations:
- Use AWS S3 compatible provider block in terraform with custom endpoint when on-prem.
- Add precondition checks: if kms_key_id != "", verify key policy allows PutObject; fail fast otherwise.

Upgrade strategy for TF modules:
- Keep old module name alias for 2 releases to allow blue/green switch (module.v1 and module.v2).
- Avoid changing persistentVolumeClaim names to prevent data loss in disk-buffer migration.
- Provide migration job that streams buffered files from old path to new path if PVC name must change.

Testing locally:
- `terraform plan -var-file=qa.tfvars` against a minikube cluster using a mock S3 endpoint (minio)
- Use `helm test` injections for the otel collector to simulate backpressure scenarios

Common pitfalls observed in previous rollouts:
- forgetting to set `s3_ca_cert` when S3 endpoint uses private CA -> TLS handshake errors in uploader
- too large queue_max_items without enough disk budget -> OOMKill during spike
- changing image_tag without warming the gateway -> client-side TLS renegotiation failures
upgrade_steps:
Pre-rollout (2 weeks out):
- Create runbook and add stakeholders to oncall list.
- Add feature flags: `new_otlp_pipeline_enabled` for each cluster.
- Prepare terraform with module.v2 alias and smoke cluster.

Canary rollout (day 0):
- 1) Deploy OTEL gateway v2 to a single region with replica_count=2 behind PDB
- 2) Enable new pipeline for a single low-traffic customer (flag=true)
- 3) Observe metrics: queue_size, send_rate, retry_rate, archive_success_rate for 4 hours
- 4) If metric regressions within threshold, continue; else revert flag and scale down v2

Scale rollout (day 1-3):
- Expand to 10% clusters, then 50% with automated checks after each step.
- Run log-archiver dry-run for 24h comparing object counts and sizes between old and new pipelines.

Fallback plan:
- Flip `new_otlp_pipeline_enabled=false` (server-side flag) -> collectors fall back to gateway v1
- If persistent failure: roll back terraform module to alias v1 and restart gateway pods gracefully

Post-upgrade (day 7):
- Run an integrity check comparing sample traces and metrics counts across windows.
- Archive audit logs for the upgrade and attach to JIRA ticket for compliance
checklist:
Pre-deployment checklist:
- [ ] Confirm backup of disk-buffer PVCs
- [ ] Validate S3 endpoint and KMS policy (test PutObject + GetObject)
- [ ] Provision canary cluster and test load generator against it
- [ ] Update Grafana provisioning to include new datasource for gateway v2
- [ ] Notify customers in the maintenance window list

Deployment checklist:
- [ ] Deploy tf module.v2 with `plan-only` first and inspect changes
- [ ] Apply in canary namespace with low traffic
- [ ] Monitor: collector_mem_rss, collector_queue_length, otel_send_errors, s3_upload_errors
- [ ] Run archive dry-run and compare counts

Post-deployment checklist:
- [ ] Promote module.v2 across namespaces in stages
- [ ] Remove legacy module alias after 2 stable releases
- [ ] File retrospective with all owners
testing_plan:
Load and reliability tests:
- Synthetic load: use vegeta-like generator for metrics and a log-flooder (10k events/min) to simulate bursts.
- Slow-network tests: run `tc qdisc netem` to introduce bandwidth limits (300Mbps, 100Mbps, 20Mbps) and validate disk-buffering and retry behavior.
- Disk-full simulation: fill 90% of disk buffer and assert eviction policy behaves as expected.

Acceptance criteria:
- No more than 1% message loss under 50k events/min sustained for 10m (with disk-buffering enabled).
- Archive success rate > 99.5% over 1h after steady-state.
- Memory usage for collector < 75% of container limit at 99p during 30m spike test.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Collector OOM during sudden bursts
Mitigation:
- Enforce resource requests/limits in module defaults
- Set `queue_max_items` conservative default and increase disk_buffer_size

Risk: S3 auth failures in customer environments
Mitigation:
- Preflight terraform check on KMS and bucket policy
- Provide a short diagnostic job that attempts PutObject and prints detailed error codes for troubleshooting

Risk: TLS handshake failures with private CA
Mitigation:
- Add `s3_ca_cert` var and test with openssl s_client in rollout checklist
